title: Does regulator set-point still beat inverter volt-var for PV hosting on the IEEE 34- and 123-node feeders?
lede: PV hosting capacity of the IEEE 34- and 123-node feeders in OpenDSS (200 random placements): on the 123-node feeder a 2 V lower regulator set-point adds +790 kW to a 1,160 kW median (every placement better), inverter volt-var +100 kW and fixed power factor +180 kW; the published 34-node case has no headroom at all because its source is set to 1.05 pu (modelled, not measured feeders); over a one-minute day the set-point trades overvoltage for undervoltage while inverter reactive power cuts tap operations about 30 %.
summary: Does the 13-node result of infra-hosting (a lower regulator set-point beats inverter reactive power) survive on larger feeders? The same OpenDSS ramp (PV added at 1–8 random customer loads until the first service voltage above 1.05 pu or transformer above its kVA rating; 200 placements, seed 1, every measure on identical placements) is run on the IEEE 123-node feeder (3,490 kW) and the 34-node feeder (1,769 kW). 123-node, load 0.3 of peak: baseline median 1,160 kW (10th–90th percentile 380–2,440); a 2 V lower set-point on all regulators +790 kW (better on 100 % of placements), fixed power factor 0.95 +180 kW (better 64 %, worse 34 %), the IEEE 1547-2018 Category B volt-var curve +100 kW (64 % / 28 %); the lowest service voltage at peak with no PV stays 0.960 pu at −2 V and falls to 0.940 at −4 V. The ranking holds, but inverter reactive power does help here, unlike on the 13-node feeder. The published 34-node case sets its source to 1.05 pu, so a regulated bus is already above 1.05 with no PV and hosting capacity is 0 for every placement and measure; with the source at 1.00 (an edit) the median is 590 kW and fixed power factor (+180) edges out the set-point (+140). Limits: snapshots, not a day; no conductor ampacities (the cases give none; worst line current at capacity is reported instead); the volt-var curve points are recalled, and the 34-node source edit is mine. Quasi-static day (added): the 123-node feeder run for a day at one-minute steps with the PV and load shapes shipped with the OpenDSS case (40 placements, 2,000 kW of PV, peak-load day): the baseline spends a median 247 min above 1.05 pu and 401 regulator tap operations; a 2 V lower set-point removes the overvoltage (0 min) but adds 193 min below 0.95 pu (baseline 11) and no fewer tap operations (412); fixed power factor 0.95 and volt-var cut overvoltage to 145 and 134 min and tap operations by about 30 % (292, 280) with no undervoltage. So the snapshot ranking reverses once undervoltage is counted. Limits: one PV shape (a cloudy day of unstated origin), regulators settle fully each minute, and some volt-var runs at 3,000 kW did not converge.
